The panels have a white frame and black photovoltaic cells with a diamond-shaped pattern.
The panels appear to be in used condition with some dust and minor surface wear.
No brand or model name is visible on the panels in either photo.
The background shows a shop with glass windows and some posters, including one with 'CANADA' visible.
The watermark 'YOUNG MIRACLE GLOBAL LINK' is visible on photo 1.

Availability is a logistical claim that cannot be verified from photos alone.
Price is not stated or shown; affordability is subjective and cannot be verified remotely.

risks.risk: The panel may not be 400W or 96 cells as claimed.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the panel's label or backside showing the rated power and cell count.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic used solar panel without verified specs, which may be lower than 400W/96 cells.

risks.risk: The panel may be counterfeit or not genuine Canadian-made.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturer's label or certification sticker on the back of the panel.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unbranded or generic, which reduces value.

risks.risk: The panel may have hidden damage or defects not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A video or photo showing the panel under sunlight with a multimeter test for voltage and current output.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially non-functional or with reduced efficiency.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the label or backside of the panel showing brand, model, and rated power (Wattage) and cell count.
Photo of the manufacturer's label or certification sticker.
Video or photo of the panel under sunlight with a multimeter test showing output voltage and current.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
